page: Microsoft Azure E32ps_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the Epsv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores powered by the Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 processor, operating at a clock speed of 3.4 GHz with a single thread per core. The processor configuration includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 128 MB of L3 cache. The server is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per core ratio, and does not include local storage or integrated GPUs.

In benchmark evaluations, the E32ps_v6 demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities and exceptional memory performance. The multi-core stress-ng and Geekbench tests place the server in the top 25% tier, while its memory bandwidth performance is top-tier, reaching 436.06 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 184.19 GB/sec for large block write operations. Database operations also rank in the top 10% according to PassMark benchmarks. However, single-core performance remains average, and large-scale LLM inference shows poor prompt processing speeds at 4.66 tokens per second, indicating a clear tradeoff between massive parallel memory throughput and single-threaded execution speed.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM-based architecture provides high resource density and memory capacity without the premium associated with traditional x86 memory-optimized instances. The high memory-to-core ratio and top-tier database benchmark scores make this server highly suitable for memory-intensive workloads, including relational databases, caching layers, and data compilation tasks. It is also well-suited for multi-threaded applications like static web serving and software compilation, though it is not recommended for heavy single-threaded processing or large-scale AI model inference.
